thread:
henry_customer: Hey team, our prod app started seeing p99 token latency jump from ~400ms to 6-8s around 09:10 UTC. A bunch of requests are timing out. Request-id: req_9a8f3c. We opened SUP-12345. Any quick ideas?

monitor-bot: Alert: service=redwood-serving cluster=eu-west-1 policy=prod p99_latency increased from 380ms to 6.2s (09:09 UTC)

eva_support: Thanks Henry — moving to support channel. Can you paste a short curl repro and confirm model/route + any recent traffic pattern changes?

henry_customer: Model: rwd/llama2-13b-v1 (hosted). Route: /v1/generate. Curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd/llama2-13b-v1","input":"<long convo...>","max_tokens":1024}'``` We saw a lot more long-context requests after a product push (more history included per request).

eva_support: Got it. Can you share a couple of full request IDs (root + a slow sample) and a rough timeline? Also the last successful request ts before spike.

henry_customer: Slow samples: req_9a8f3c, req_9a8f5d, req_9a90aa. Last normal was ~09:03 UTC.

kai_runtime: Looping in runtime. From grafana quick look: around 09:08 we see a sharp rise in per-GPU device mem_used and kv_cache_bytes. p95->p99 increases line up with kv cache growth on nodes serving that model. Might be per-request KV retention > TTL.

sam_sre: Any deploys around then?

deploy-bot: deploy: serving:release/2026.03.10-11 triggered at 09:05 UTC by @ci-bot (hash abc123)

kai_runtime: That deploy touched a change in prefix caching: default keep_history=true for shared sessions. If customers send full conversation on every request that could blow up KV cache per session. Seeing many sessions with kv_cache_bytes ~8-12GB each on ~A100 nodes — causing host-level fragmentation and allocator pressure.

eva_support: So probable cause = KV growth from long history retention + deploy default change. Immediate ask: can you temporarily route traffic to a non-affected pool or reduce history size per request?

henry_customer: We can reduce history, but want a short-term mitigation while we roll that. Any runtime hotfix?

kai_runtime: Mitigations we can try now: 1) Restart serving pods on affected nodes to drop per-process KV caches (low risk, short outage per pod). 2) Toggle keep_history=false at routing layer for that customer (we can patch routing policy). 3) Apply allocator tuning: enable jemalloc background thread or reduce per-thread arenas — but that's a config change requiring restart. 4) Force eviction for stale kv entries via admin endpoint: `POST /admin/kv/evict?age_secs=300&route=customer-henry` — I'll check permissions.

sam_sre: Rolling restarts sound fastest. We should avoid cluster-wide reboots. We'll do canary restart on 2 pods first. Also open firewall for network drain to balance.

kai_runtime: Running quick check on node logs: ```[09:09:12] gpu0: total=40960MiB free=2048MiB used=38912MiB
[09:09:12] kv_cache_bytes=11953748992
[09:09:12] allocator: fragmentation=0.58 slabs=128 active=73MB
[09:09:13] p99_latency=6231ms
``` Fragmentation ratio >0.5 and kv_cache ~11.9GB looks bad. If allocator can't get contiguous blocks, allocations stall and we see p99 spikes.

eva_support: Kai, can you confirm whether garbage collection/eviction is blocked by long-lived goroutines or stuck sessions?

kai_runtime: Traces show many goroutines in kv::pin_and_hold waiting on backoffs. There's a race where keep_history retains KV refs until full request finish; when many concurrent long requests, KV growth outpaces eviction.

henry_customer: If we reduce concurrency from our side for a few mins would that help?

sam_sre: Yes throttling client concurrency will help short term. Henry — can you rate-limit to ~25% of peak for 15–30 minutes while we roll?

henry_customer: We can try. Doing a staged throttle now.

monitor-bot: Notice: p99 latency dropped to ~900ms after initial throttling (09:20 UTC).

kai_runtime: Good signal. We'll still do a targeted canary restart on two pods in the serving pool now to release KV caches and reduce fragmentation. Expect brief 5–10s cold starts per pod.

sam_sre: Performing canary restart: pod/serve-a-12 -> terminating -> started (09:25 UTC). Pod/serve-b-03 next.

monitor-bot: Pod restart events: serve-a-12 restarted (09:26 UTC). p99 down to 420ms.

henry_customer: After restart latency looks back to normal for a bit. Thanks. What's next to avoid recurrence?

kai_runtime: Short-term: 1) Patch routing policy to set keep_history=false for that customer's route by default; 2) Add auto-evict admin endpoint to run when per-route kv_cache_bytes > threshold; 3) Revert default change in deploy that made keep_history true global. Medium-term: implement per-session KV caps, better LRU eviction and background defrag/compaction for our allocator.

eva_support: We'll open a PR for a revert and a support patch to add route-level override. Henry, we'll also credit you for the interruption and help craft guidance to avoid sending full convo blobs every request.

henry_customer: Appreciate that. Also would love an option to set per-call param to disable history (client-side) to avoid this in future.

kai_runtime: Adding that to backlog. For now I've invoked admin evict on the remaining nodes for that route: ```POST /admin/kv/evict?route=henry-prod&max_bytes=5000000000``` Result: evicted ~6.2GB across nodes. p99 now stable ~380ms.

sam_sre: Followups: - ticket SUP-12345 updated with runbook - create monitoring alert for kv_cache_bytes per-route > 6GB - schedule allocator tuning spike (jemalloc background thread + reduce arenas) behind a config flag - add per-route cap + auto-evict feature request

eva_support: I'll keep this thread updated and loop in product for UX change (disable history param). Thanks everyone, marking incident as mitigation in place. :white_check_mark: 

henry_customer: Thanks all, will keep throttled for 10 more minutes and then test ramp.

monitor-bot: p99 latency steady at 360-450ms (10:02 UTC). Incident mitigated but followups remain.
